exposure: vaginal birth after cesarean (VBAC) under epidural anesthesia
cohort: The study included 156 term singleton VBAC cases with epidural anesthesia, matched 1:1 by age to nulliparous controls.
finding: VBAC cases under epidural anesthesia had significantly higher median 24 h postpartum blood loss, postpartum hemorrhage rates, and neonatal NICU admission rates compared to nulliparous controls.
mod_finding: VBAC under epidural anesthesia may progress faster through the first and second stages of labor than nulliparous deliveries but carries higher risks of adverse outcomes.
